output.title: Privacy terms do not control your workflow
output.body:
If you are a small business owner trying AI for the first time, privacy promises are only part of the decision. A vendor can tell you where data sits, how it is protected, and what terms apply. That still does not answer the bigger operational question: who is allowed to act on the data once it enters your workflow?

The bounded decision is simple. For a repeatable process like invoice handling or customer replies, decide whether the AI may take an action on its own, or whether it only recommends an action and waits for human approval. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. That is Bareni policy, not a slogan.

Privacy matters. But it does not replace your own control design. If the approval path is loose, the vendor’s privacy terms will not fix that. If the approval path is tight, you can use AI without handing over the keys to the shop.

One practical check is this: will I see the input, the reasoning, and the recommended action before anything is committed?

Next, map your most repeated workflow and mark the points where money, customer communication, or data deletion could happen. Then decide which of those points must remain human-approved.
